title: Restore egress resolver affinity after peering flip to prevent cross-tenant DNS bleed
creator: Asha Raman
description: Large enterprise customer reported intermittent leakage of private hostnames into other tenants immediately after VPC peering failover during a Dedicated capacity scale event. Symptoms: cross-tenant A-record answers and stale resolver responses for ~30-120s after a peering flip, causing client cert mismatches and application errors. Root cause analysis indicates the resolver affinity index (a small in-memory mapping keyed by tenant->egress-binding-id) was not being atomically rotated during the peering handover. On peering swap the control plane updated routing quickly but the data-plane resolver affinity table held stale egress bindings while ephemeral SNAT ports and per-tenant connection tracking were being recycled, producing misdirected DNS responses. Contributing factors: (1) resolver affinity reconciliation runs are scheduled at low priority with a 60s jitter; (2) controller applies peering changes before we drain/rotate egress-binding indices; (3) a recent optimization to avoid full affinity table rewrites introduced a race when the primary egress interface index changed during a mid-transaction peering update. This ticket implements a production-safe fix, tests, and a roll-forward rollout plan to eliminate the leakage window and provide a fast mitigation path for escalations.
